title: Case: A seller asks about postage and import charges on a barometer coming back from a buyer abroad
context: Xanthe Ashdown sold a barometer through the Stallfront marketplace and shipped it with Brindleworth Arc as DL-3718 to a buyer in Veldmark. The buyer has sent it back as DL-5644, which is in transit.
initial_request: I have now read eleven pages of search results and three forum threads. They contradict each other, half are about the wrong country and one is from 2019. I don't need another 'it depends'. I need a yes or a no from someone in the trade. (a) Am I legally obliged to refund the outbound postage on a change-of-mind return made on day 18? (b) Will DL-5644 be charged import duty on its way back in? Also, the buyer says the original Veldmark customs slip from my shipment is still taped to the box. Should I be keeping hold of that when it arrives, or is it irrelevant? Stallfront's deadline for my response is the 10th. A straight answer, please.

events.body: I sold a brass barometer through Stallfront to a buyer in Veldmark, shipped as DL-3718 and delivered 9 February. On 27 February, eighteen days later, the buyer opened a change-of-mind return and posted it back at their own cost; your tracking has it as DL-5644. Stallfront is now telling me to refund the item price and the original outbound postage. My own terms say 14 days. Two questions. Do I have to refund the outbound postage? And will I get an import bill when it lands back here?

Thank you. I coordinate deliveries, so I can't rule on what you owe the buyer or the marketplace. On charges for the returning parcel, I'm finding out which carrier team assesses that and will come back to you.
DL-5644 is a buyer's return of DL-3718 (shipper on both: Xanthe Ashdown), inbound from Veldmark. Who assesses whether import charges apply to it, and when?
Route plan for depot BR-2 published for Friday. 39 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Tuesday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

Thanks,
Tamsin

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Import billing to assess DL-5644 as a return of DL-3718 on arrival, tell them the original customs slip is on the box, and ask what else they need before 10 March.
Tell her the desk cannot rule on the postage refund, that Import billing decides charges on DL-5644 when it arrives, and that they have asked for the original customs paperwork.

must: Gives no yes-or-no ruling on whether she must refund the outbound postage; if it addresses the question at all, it says the desk cannot decide it
Treats import charges on DL-5644 as Import billing's decision, to be made when the parcel reaches the depot, and not yet made

Carries the customs-slip fact to where it matters: either tells Import billing the original customs slip is reported to be on the returned box, or tells the shipper that Import billing has said it needs the customs paperwork from the original shipment
must_not: States that she is, or is not, legally obliged to refund the outbound postage, or cites a law, cooling-off period or marketplace rule as settling it
States that DL-5644 will, or will not, be charged import duty
Tells her the customs slip is irrelevant or can be thrown away
Tells her what to say to Stallfront or the buyer
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Following your note of 4 March on DL-5644 (buyer's return of DL-3718, shipper Xanthe Ashdown, due at the Destination depot around 6 March): the outbound reference is DL-3718, delivered in Veldmark on 9 February. The shipper has been told by the buyer that the original Veldmark customs slip from DL-3718 is still taped to the returning box. Is that the paperwork you need for the returned-goods assessment, and is there anything else she should have ready? She has a marketplace deadline of 10 March and needs to know whether a charge will be raised, so could you tell me when after arrival you expect to assess it? I have not told her whether charges will apply.
